atoms.a: A member of which country in the UK does this person represent?
Which characteristic(s) of an English Person can be interpreted from this image?

atoms.b:
Whilst the English person identifies as British, the other three people each express ((++two one three)) national identities. All four state that they identify as ((++British English Welsh)), but three of them strongly identify with their individual countries. Thus, a difference across the UK in terms of national and ((++regional individualistic international)) identity is portrayed here.
Further, it suggests that “Britishness” and “Englishness” may be understood as ((++synonyms opposites contrasts)) because to the English person it is sufficient to express that they are British rather than English and British. Overall, strong regional identities outside ((++England the_UK Britain)) are pictured and raise a question of what it means to identify as British.

atoms.text: The English Gentleman and the English attributes are largely in the middle of the picture, while the three other nation's representatives are at the sides and no cultural attributes are shown, besides the countries' flags. An interpretation suggests that the perception of “Britishness” is largely anglocentric.

b: setting a focus on the Anglican church
++centered on or prioritising England or English things

atoms.text: Lastly, the Palace of Westminster (Houses of Parliament) in the right-hand corner is the centre of British politics and is in London, England.

atoms.a: What does this add to the interpretation?
b: ++The fact that political debate essentially happens in England adds to the image of Britain and Britishness centred around England.
British politics do not play a role in British identity formation.
Overall, representation of all countries which make up the UK in the concept of Britishness is equal.
